evidence: InternalTimecodeSource now uses a dedicated bundled module worker instead of requestAnimationFrame. It samples the monotonic elapsed clock at 60 Hz and emits changed frames up to 30 fps. Sampling at twice the maximum frame rate avoids timer jitter reducing fresh output to roughly 27–28 fps. Unsupported/failed module workers use a cancellable interval fallback; browser suspension remains subject to the relay feed watchdog.

useTimecode sends fresh internal observations directly instead of batching them through the old 100ms interval. MTC flushes fresh observations on a 30 Hz worker and never repeats its last input to hide signal loss. Pause, Stop, disconnect, ownership loss and scope changes cancel local schedulers; resume starts at the relay's exact held frame. A failed first feed cannot leave the UI claiming generator ownership.

Regressions cover all four frame formats, exact held-frame resume, no animation dependency, coalesced tick deduplication, worker replacement on repeated seeks, fallback and cleanup, roughly 30 fresh internal frames per second, disconnect and failed-start handling.
